## Active development policy â€” owner-directed acceleration (2026-09-10)

The owner directs necessary policy changes going forward so this integration is quick and efficient. This prospective section governs development of this single combined app and supersedes only the conflicting serial-development, single-correction, per-card reexecution and whole-checkout-freeze process clauses identified here, whether below or inherited. It does not amend frozen product contracts, historical acceptance or owner-only release boundaries. The owner-approved 2026-09-23 amendment below changes only prospective review/provider/noncritical-visual gate placement; complete functionality, data safety and critical journeys remain required. The earlier diagnosis, path lists, runs and reviews below remain immutable chronology, not repeated work orders.

### Work in integration batches, not miniature card cycles

- Organize remaining work by dependency: populated-store migration/recovery; one production lifecycle and real feature routes; Phase 10 adoption on those routes; final combined verification. Independent work may proceed concurrently. A provisional card does not require a separate authority commit, native run or ceremony merely because its number precedes another card. Preserve every card's requirement/disposition and dependency semantics in the final coverage reconciliation; do not manufacture individual accepted receipts.
- Before a workstream's first edit, record its concrete requirement, exact fully expanded existing file paths, source evidence, preserved invariants, owner, shared-contract boundaries, paired tests, expected evidence/selectors and dependency/predecessor checkpoint in this task. Several compatible causal corrections may share that finite workset and one reviewed checkpoint. A causal neighboring declaration, caller or paired test requires a short source-grounded explicit addition before its edit, not a new owner question or a standalone authority commit. New production files/resources/project changes still require explicit causal scope rather than this neighbor rule. This is not blanket permission over directories, unrelated features or unowned files. Commit the scope record with the implementation it governs.
- Reuse existing implementers with disjoint file ownership and one independent integration reviewer. The root is the single committer, preserving direct-child linear correction history after the already recorded source merge. One owner integrates shared contracts; dependent lanes may use an agreed interface but cannot invent stubs, a parallel architecture or a second writer. Resolve consequential interface questions before parallel implementation. Review actual combined changes incrementally, retaining prior findings until their source or dependency contract changes.
- Use one concise checkpoint per meaningful batch: requirement/path map, actual changes, review, checks, exact native question and remaining gaps. Keep detailed compiler output and file checksums in the original evidence, not repeatedly copied into authority prose. Append HANDOFF at meaningful verification/integration boundaries; do not create an implementation/authority/handoff commit triplet for each small repair.

### Keep useful work moving while CI runs

- A dispatched commit, its inputs and original artifacts are immutable; the local working tree is not globally frozen during a development diagnostic. After confirming the run's exact head/ref and checkout identity, prepare and review a descendant while that original run completes. Non-force pushing a descendant is permitted only after the original checkout/source binding is confirmed and no consumer resolves mutable branch bytes. Original results remain evidence for their own head, never for the descendant.
- Do not queue speculative replacement runs, duplicate a question/shard, cancel a run, rerun a failed run ID, or dispatch a known unchanged deterministic failure. The descendant diagnostic waits for its predecessor diagnostic to be terminal and its original evidence to be audited once; do not infer a failure from unfinished output. Independent source-proven corrections and implementation do not wait for an unrelated run to finish. If a run is already active, use its result instead of launching the same question again.
- Before each batch mutation, commit/push or dispatch, refresh the facts that can change: ownership/dirty state, relevant refs and, for dispatch, live capacity and exact inputs. Reuse verified frozen authority readings, source inventories, review results and deterministic-check results only while their actual inputs and commands remain unchanged. A changed relevant digest invalidates that result. Do not rerun unchanged broad scans or re-read the entire historical program on every small edit.

### Right-size development tests; preserve final coverage

- Each development dispatch answers one stated question using the smallest useful source-defined test set and the existing supported N8, P12 or F25 tier. The development selector may focus on the changed dependency closure rather than accumulating all earlier methods into every run. No test is deleted, disabled, weakened or marked passing because it was not selected. The existing 33-method set at `e68a1e5f78de29edf2dd381f93875eff28ea31d0` is the minimum retained regression seed, augmented by every later accepted causal regression and the complete retained dependency/journey inventory; it is not a final coverage ceiling. Causally corrected methods carry the same semantic obligations.
- Run supported deterministic source checks before hosted work. Use compiler diagnostics to repair compatible errors as a reviewed batch. A source-proven blocker in the selected question is fixed first; there is no run merely to rediscover it. Storage, writer, recovery, report/media, entitlement and data-rights changes require their affected native dependency-closure tests, not only a fresh empty-store smoke. The complete required compatibility corpus and retained essential journeys remain due on the final candidate.
- Derive current-runtime affected states from actual wired screens and risk, using continuous journeys/shared-layout representatives. Critical functional, privacy and accessibility journeys plus their genuine human review precede merge. Explicitly listed noncritical cosmetic polish may follow merge but must be reviewed before release. Preserve every obligation and the existing minimum-runtime/physical deferrals; no automatic historical-state replay.
- One collector owns each original run. Verify its complete original integrity once, preserve its failures/warnings and reuse the verified local hashes. Recheck live ownership/expiry or newly changed evidence when relevant; do not duplicate downloads and unchanged full audits. Compilation, selected-unit success, UI progress, visual review and formal acceptance remain distinct claims.

### Native route, review binding and final freeze — owner approved 2026-09-23

Each consequential batch receives one independent semantic review of the complete affected contract after focused deterministic input/environment, mode, selector and real-entry checks. Long regressions may run concurrently with read-only review; both must pass before adoption, commit or dispatch. Only noncritical visual polish may remain after merge, with each item explicitly recorded in VERIFICATION_DUE and completed with genuine human review before release. ### Audited originals36093018041/36093046826/36093079109 (fca18b7, D2)

All three compiled with 0 Swift errors (498 warnings) and were sole-collected with the named-diagnostic summary.
- Mount exact7: 2/7. The acknowledgement-loss recovery journey now passes, and so does the foreign-draft denial. Four Continue failures are named `step=launch-prepare` or `step=entry-prepare` with `ScanToWorkFailureV1.notReady`, thrown by `prepareRepetitiveCaptureLaunch`/`prepareRepetitiveCaptureStep` after `rebuildReadiness` succeeded. The denial method's direct launch prints `V23_ROUND_STEP_FAILURE step=prepare-launch-0 … notReady`; its reported `resourceValueMismatch` is the XCTest misattribution. The revision-pinned method fails separately (`XCTAssertNil` on a UUID, then no `ProductionRepetitiveCaptureReadV2`).
- Completion exact12: 7/12. The six readiness methods and the storage predicate pass. All five journeys fail at the same `launch-prepare`/`entry-prepare` `notReady`.
- Startup exact3: 2/3. The swallowed error is `FinalizationServiceError.journalFailed` (committed=false). The injected advance failure fires, yet the live finalization, staging and final snapshot directories are empty.

Startup cause (root trace, fca18b7): the test builds `ProductionCheckRunnerItemDraftServiceV1` over a plain `CheckRunnerCoordinator` with no live operation, so `FinalizationService` takes the non-live store path (`FinalizationService.swift:559-589`). There, `advanceUnprotected` consumes `.intentPhaseWrite(.snapshotPromoted)` and calls `rollbackUncommittedUnprotected` (`FinalizationIntentStore.swift:1123-1126`, since 43ef739), which removes the promoted snapshot, the staging copy and the prepared journal before throwing. The service reports `journalFailed`. This in-process rollback is the designed non-live behavior; the live path (`advanceLive`) deliberately keeps a valid prepared journal. The test's uncommitted branch therefore does not exercise the crash-like state it names. Correction due in the next C36 batch: drive the finalization through the live operation path used by the production Round host (as `testLiveFinalizationUsesOriginalReceiptAndRejectsRetiredOperation` does), keeping every assertion. `S3_4ResumeRecoveryTests.testCurrentV2PreparedPromotedAndCommittedInterruptionsRecoverThroughNewWriter` expects the same injection to leave a prepared journal on the non-live path and has no native timing; the coverage sweep will show whether it fails since 43ef739. The `notReady` Continue guard remains under read-only diagnosis.

### Readiness source drift binds the storage verdict (batch F, 2026-09-25)

Requirement (source-proven): a Round Continue must not fail because free space moved between the two reads of one readiness rebuild. `OfflineReadinessPreflightCoordinatorV1.rebuild` reduces its second read against the first, and `OfflineReadinessManifestSourceProofV1.Basis` hashed the full storage observation including live `availableBytes`, so any movement made the manifest `.stale`, `mayStartFieldWork` false and `ScanToWorkContractsV1.swift:70` threw `notReady`. This matched every failing Continue in 36093018041/36093046826. Commit 2abaa1d had corrected only final publication (`supportsPublication`).

Envelope (root-owned):
- `FieldEvidenceApp/Domain/OfflineReadiness/OfflineReadinessManifestContractsV1.swift`: the source-proof basis hashes a `StorageVerdict` (capacity state, both reservations, and whether checked capacity covers the mandatory requirement plus reservations; nil when unchecked or on overflow). The manifest still records the observed bytes in its own digest.
- `FieldEvidenceAppTests/V9_71OfflineReadinessManifestTests.swift`: `testStorageFreeByteDriftIsNotSourceDriftButEveryVerdictChangeIs`.
- `FieldEvidenceAppTests/V9_104MyDayWorkflowTests.swift`: the byte-exact drift test is replaced by `testProductionMyDayReadinessUsesCapacityVerdictDriftSemantics` (ample drift stays ready; a verdict flip between reads is drift; a late verdict flip at publication is still `sourcesChanged`).

Shared interfaces: the manifest is `DERIVED_ONLY`; the digest is compared only within one build (Scan-to-Work proof, repetitive capture draft proof), and no fixture pins it. Lighting C17/C18 hash full storage separately and share the defect; they have no production caller and remain due.

## Release blocker: S10 → V23 upgrade digest (2026-09-25; decided, implementation queued)

Measured natively (development only, iOS 26.5 Simulator):
- The real S10 path runs a legacy pointer from release .v1, then aggregate steps V1→V53. Every step from V3 up hashes a nested `semanticExportVn` that embeds Vn-1 as base64, so it grows by exactly 4/3 per layer.
  - Empty store: 29 MB at V40, 289 MB at V48, about 1.2 GB predicted at V53.
  - A V1 store with 1 site: openForStartup completed in 316 s with more than 2.1 GB RSS.
  - A V1 store with 40 sites: killed at 660 s while still at V46 to V47, with RSS up to 7.3 GB. It would not complete on a device (jetsam).
- The existing framed digest (`StoreSemanticLayerDigestV1`) takes 7–14 ms on the same data.

Decision (root, owner decisions 14 and 18):
- The aggregate migration path moves to framed layered digests: adjacent source and target checks, the prior projection, the final candidate and published-target validation. `StoreSemanticLayerDigestV1` extends to V3…V53, and existing V53 framed bytes stay identical.
- V1/V2 flat source digests stay frozen in the journal, per `semanticDigestPolicy`.
- The final aggregate manifest is written as schema 2 with framed layers.
- The aggregate journal digest format is marked explicitly, so an in-flight nested journal fails closed with forwardFixRequired.

Evidence: the blueprint requires bounded memory (:11716, :11822) and forward-migratable shipped schemas (:11323), and says new framed forms get a new version or domain and never reinterpret released bytes (:394, :514). The registry `semanticDigestPolicy` doesn't mandate a nested form.

Format impact: no shipped store. S10 is V1 and has no digests; V2–V52 never shipped. Development V53 stores with schema-1 manifests stay readable, because V53 open doesn't re-hash them.

Proof required:
- the real V1 openForStartup (1 site and 40+ sites) completes both launches under a time and memory budget;
- V10_01 v4/v9 aggregates;
- framed layer, tamper and count tests;
- rejection of old-format journals;
- schema-2 manifest validation.

This is a restricted migration change: independent review and all five gates.

Separate item: S3_4 `testOriginalRecoveryThroughActiveUpgrade…` fails in 3.3 s before migration, with route maintenance(eraseInconsistent).
